deep.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar
deep.score_reason: Google DeepMind 发布 Gemini 3.8 Live 带 Live Avatar，新一代旗舰模型发布，直接影响应用选型。
deep.analysis:
这是 Google DeepMind 在 2026 年 9 月发布的 Gemini 3.8 Live 版本，核心亮点是引入了“Live Avatar”——一个能实时生成面部表情、唇形同步、头部姿态和手势的虚拟形象，与 Gemini 的语音对话能力深度耦合，形成完整的“听得见、看得着”的交互体验。

此前，大模型的语音交互虽然已经做到低延迟、可打断，但用户面对的始终是一个“黑盒声音”。在客服、教育、虚拟陪伴等场景中，缺乏视觉反馈会让交互显得生硬、信任感不足。传统做法是事后用 TTS 驱动 3D 模型，但语音和表情异步、唇形对不上、手势机械重复，整体观感割裂。Gemini 3.8 Live 要解决的核心痛点，就是将语音理解和视觉表达放在同一个推理循环里，让虚拟形象的表情动作成为模型原生输出的一部分，而不是后期拼凑。

技术实现上，这套系统有三个关键设计。第一，Gemini 3.8 本身是一个多模态原生模型，它在输出语音 token 的同时，会并行输出“avatar token”——一组描述面部 blendshape 权重、头部旋转角、手势类别和身体姿态的离散控制信号。Blendshape 是 3D 动画里用来混合不同面部表情的技术，模型直接预测这些权重值，就能驱动虚拟形象做出自然的表情变化。第二，整个流程在单一推理循环中完成，语音 token 和 avatar token 共享同一个上下文窗口，这意味着模型在决定“说什么”的时候，已经知道“该做什么表情”，唇形和语音天然同步，不需要额外的对齐模块。第三，Live Avatar 支持流式渲染，avatar token 以 25fps 的帧率持续输出，配合 Gemini Live 已有的低延迟语音管线，端到端延迟控制在可接受范围内，用户看到的虚拟形象能实时响应对话内容，点头、挑眉、手势等非语言信号与语义高度相关。

对 AI 应用岗而言，这条资讯至少有三个可谈的面试点。一是“多模态输出的工程化”，过去我们习惯讨论多模态输入（图文音），但 Gemini 3.8 Live 展示的是多模态输出的产品形态——模型不仅生成文本和语音，还直接生成视觉行为，这要求面试者理解 token 化表示如何扩展到非语言模态，以及流式解码如何同步多种模态的时序。二是“实时交互系统的延迟预算”，语音对话本身有严格延迟要求，叠加 avatar 渲染后，如何在模型推理、网络传输、客户端渲染之间分配延迟预算，是生产环境中必须考虑的工程问题。三是“虚拟形象在 AI 应用中的产品价值”，可以结合面试岗位讨论：在智能客服、在线教育、虚拟直播等场景中，有表情反馈的 AI 形象如何提升用户留存和信任度，以及这类功能的技术成本与收益权衡。如果面试官问到对 Gemini 新版本的看法，可以从“原生多模态输出”这个角度切入，说明你理解这不仅是功能叠加，而是模型架构层面的演进。

deep.title: Better prompt caching for GPT-6
deep.summary: Learn how GPT-6 improves prompt caching with higher cache hit rates, new diagnostics, explicit breakpoints, and controls that reduce latency and costs.
deep.score_reason: GPT-6 prompt caching 改进（命中率、诊断、断点控制），直接影响延迟和成本，工程实用性强。
deep.analysis:
在 OpenAI 最新发布的 GPT-6 技术更新中，一项名为“更好的提示缓存”的功能被正式推出。简单来说，提示缓存是一种让模型记住之前处理过的提示前缀（即对话或请求中重复出现的开头部分）的技术，从而避免对相同内容重复计算，直接复用之前的结果。GPT-6 对这一机制进行了系统性升级，带来了更高的缓存命中率、全新的诊断工具、显式断点以及更精细的控制手段，最终目标是降低延迟和成本。

此前，大语言模型在处理连续对话或批量请求时，即使提示的前半部分完全相同，模型仍需从头到尾完整计算，这造成了算力和时间的浪费。早期的缓存机制虽然尝试解决这个问题，但存在两个明显痛点：一是缓存命中率不稳定，开发者无法预知或控制哪些内容会被缓存；二是缺乏可观测性，当缓存未命中时，开发者无从得知原因，只能被动接受更高的延迟和费用。对于需要高频调用、长上下文或严格成本控制的生产环境，这种不确定性是一个工程上的硬伤。

GPT-6 的改进从三个层面入手解决上述问题。第一，通过算法优化提升了缓存命中率，让更多语义相近或结构相似的提示前缀能够被准确识别并复用，而不仅仅是基于字符串的严格匹配。第二，新增了诊断功能，开发者现在可以查看每次请求的缓存命中情况，理解哪些部分被缓存、哪些没有，以及原因是什么，这为性能调优提供了数据支撑。第三，也是最具工程价值的一点，是引入了“显式断点”和更细粒度的控制。开发者可以在提示中主动标记缓存边界，明确告诉模型“到这里为止的内容可以缓存，之后的内容需要重新计算”。这意味着缓存策略从过去的黑盒自动化，变成了可编程、可预测的基础设施能力。结合这些控制手段，开发者能够针对特定应用场景（如长文档问答、多轮对话系统）精细地划分缓存区域，最大化复用计算成果。

对于 AI 应用岗的面试和实际工作，这条更新有几点值得深入思考。首先，它体现了大模型从“模型能力竞赛”向“工程化落地”转变的趋势——降低成本和延迟不再是算法团队的内部优化，而是通过可编程接口暴露给应用层开发者，成为系统设计的一部分。面试中如果被问到“如何优化大模型应用的响应速度与成本”，你可以从缓存策略切入，具体谈到显式断点的设计思路：将系统提示、少样本示例、固定上下文等静态部分放在断点之前，将用户输入、动态数据等可变部分放在断点之后，从而在保证灵活性的同时最大化缓存收益。其次，诊断功能的加入意味着生产环境中对模型行为的可观测性要求正在向传统后端服务看齐，这涉及到监控、告警和成本归因等运维话题，是面试中展示工程素养的好角度。最后，这种将底层能力通过可控接口暴露的模式，也预示着未来 AI 应用架构中会出现更多“缓存层”“路由层”等中间件设计，对应用工程师的系统抽象能力提出了更高要求。

deep.title: Just-in-Time Memory: Learning to Curate Task-Adaptive Memory for LLM Agents
deep.summary: Agentic memory systems reuse past experience to improve future performance, yet most existing designs curate memory at write time: once a task is completed, its trajectory is distilled into a fixed artifact, such as a reflection, workflow, skill, or reasoning strategy, that is later retrieved by similarity. This forces the system to decide what is worth remembering before the future query is known, irreversibly discarding information and producing a query-independent summary that must serve many possible downstream tasks. Learning such a write-time curator is also difficult because the value of a storage decision may only become apparent when a relevant query arrives, potentially many tasks later, creating a long-horizon credit-assignment problem. We instead retain raw trajectories and defer curation until read time, when the current task is known. Given the retrieved traces and the new task, a memory curator synthesizes a compact, task-adaptive payload tailored to the immediate need. Because this payload is consumed on the same task, the curator can be trained directly from immediate task success, avoiding delayed utility signals and the need to artificially group related tasks. deep.analysis:
这是一篇关于大模型智能体记忆系统的新研究，提出了一种从“写入时整理”转向“读取时合成”的记忆管理范式。

此前的智能体记忆系统普遍采用“写入时整理”策略：任务完成后立即将完整执行轨迹压缩为固定的抽象产物，比如反思总结、工作流模板或推理策略，后续通过相似度检索复用。这种设计存在两个根本性痛点。第一是信息不可逆丢失，系统必须在知道未来查询需求之前就决定什么值得记住，一旦压缩完成，原始轨迹中的细节就被丢弃了，而后续任务可能恰好需要那些被丢弃的信息。第二是训练信号延迟，写入时的存储决策到底有没有价值，要等到未来某个相关查询出现时才能验证，这个时间跨度可能跨越多个任务，形成了典型的长期信用分配难题，让基于学习的记忆筛选器极难训练。

这项工作的核心思路是把记忆整理从写入时推迟到读取时。系统不再对原始轨迹做提前压缩，而是完整保留所有执行轨迹。当新任务到来时，先用检索找出相关历史轨迹，然后由一个记忆合成器根据当前任务的具体需求，动态生成一份紧凑且任务自适应的信息载荷。这个合成器之所以能有效训练，关键在于它生成的载荷就在同一个任务上被消费，因此可以直接用当前任务的成功与否作为训练信号，完全绕开了延迟奖励和人工分组相关任务的问题。具体实现上，记忆合成器本质上是一个语言模型，输入是检索到的原始轨迹和当前任务描述，输出是针对当前任务提炼的关键信息，这个输出会作为上下文拼接到智能体的推理过程中。训练时采用强化学习，奖励函数直接基于任务完成度，因为信号即时可得，训练变得可行且高效。

对AI应用岗而言，这项工作在工程落地和面试讨论中都有直接价值。从生产可用性看，它解决了一个非常实际的工程矛盾：记忆系统既要保留足够细节以应对未知需求，又要控制上下文长度以控制推理成本和延迟。JitMem的读取时合成策略提供了一个优雅的折中，不需要预设任务类型，不需要人工设计压缩规则，系统自动学会针对每个具体查询提取最相关的信息。在面试场景中，可以讨论的点包括：记忆系统的读写分离架构设计、长期信用分配问题在智能体系统中的具体表现、如何通过改变训练信号的获取时机来简化强化学习问题、以及这种设计与检索增强生成的关系与区别。特别值得注意的是，论文提到即使未经训练的合成器也能带来提升，说明这种架构本身就具有归纳偏置优势，这对快速原型验证很有启发。

mid.title: MILO: Efficient Many-shot In-Context Learning with Block-wise Low-rank Compression
mid.summary: Many-shot in-context learning (ICL) enables large language models (LLMs) to adapt to complex tasks by conditioning on thousands of demonstration examples, but this paradigm shifts the inference efficiency bottleneck to the key-value (KV) cache memory. Due to the linear scaling behavior of the KV cache, storing these intermediate tensors has become a paramount challenge for both online serving and on-device deployment. To address this issue, we propose a novel compression framework, termed MILO, that exploits the low-rank redundancy inherent in many-shot contexts. Specifically, MILO features a block-wise low-rank compression strategy that compresses the KV cache at the block granularity, where each block contains multiple many-shot examples. Furthermore, to handle the heterogeneous context density across different blocks, MILO dynamically allocates rank budgets based on the information entropy, preserving the fidelity of critical blocks while aggressively compressing redundant ones. Experimental results on Qwen2.5 models demonstrate that our method achieves up to 50% reduction in KV cache memory and 1.8x throughput improvement, with negligible performance degradation on classification and reasoning benchmarks, significantly outperforming prior baselines.
mid.score_reason: 解决 many-shot ICL 的 KV cache 瓶颈，低秩压缩方法对长上下文推理工程有直接价值
mid.analysis: MILO 是一种面向多示例上下文学习场景的 KV 缓存压缩框架，核心方法是对 KV 缓存进行分块低秩压缩，并根据各块的信息熵动态分配秩预算，以保留关键块的高保真度。该技术针对的是在输入数千个示例时 KV 缓存线性增长带来的内存瓶颈，旨在提升推理效率。实验表明，在 Qwen2.5 模型上，MILO 可将 KV 缓存内存减少最高 50%、吞吐量提升 1.8 倍，且分类与推理基准上的性能退化可忽略不计，显著优于此前基线方法。

paper.title: IterSynth: Rethinking Deep Search Agents via Role-Decoupled Iterative Synthesis
paper.summary: Deep search requires LLM agents to decompose complex queries, search for evidence, and synthesize grounded answers, yet existing ReAct-style agents suffer from two limitations: role coupling, where one policy must handle planning, evidence use, and synthesis; and context accumulation, where growing search histories introduce noise and obscure useful information. Experiments on five long-horizon deep-search benchmarks such as BrowseComp and Xbench-DS show that IterSynth-8B achieves an average score of 50.7, surpassing the strongest prior $\leq$8B agent by +4.2\%. Moreover, IterSynth serves as a model-agnostic prompting paradigm, delivering substantial zero-shot gains over ReAct and similar prompting paradigms on frontier proprietary models.

paper.title: Risk-Controlled KV-Cache Eviction: From Memory Budgets to Risk Targets
paper.summary: KV-cache eviction is typically evaluated through average quality-memory trade-offs, yet a small average loss can hide requests whose utility degrades materially. We reformulate eviction as a deployment risk-control problem: a material degradation occurs when eviction lowers task utility by more than a deployment-specified tolerance relative to full-KV inference on the same request, and deployment risk is the population frequency of such events. Given a reliability contract specifying a target risk level and confidence requirement, we use a compressor-agnostic post-hoc certification procedure to select a retention policy from calibration data with a finite-sample guarantee, falling back to full KV when no compressed policy is certified. Across multiple eviction methods, Llama and Mistral models, and LongBench and RULER-32K, the same contract supports substantially different levels of eviction: on Llama, it certifies SnapKV at 75% retention on LongBench but no tested compressed policy on RULER-32K, triggering full-KV fallback. Policies with empirical degradation rates below the 5% target can still fail finite-sample certification; on Llama LongBench, empirical thresholding selects uncertified policies that retain 5-10 percentage points less cache across fixed-budget methods. The proposed framework converts a deployment-level reliability requirement into a KV-memory operating point.

paper.title: Can One Adapted Model Do It All? Fine-Tuning Strategy Selection for Customer Support LLMs
paper.summary: Production customer-support systems often require LLMs to support multiple skills, such as intent classification, question answering, summarization, or tool-use decisions. We study this question using thirteen models spanning five families (Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Gemma-3, Llama-3.1, and Mistral) from 0.6B to 32B parameters across eight customer-support datasets, spanning four public and four proprietary datasets with approximately 74.5k training and 8.7k evaluation samples. Under a fixed training protocol, we train more than 200 checkpoints. Our experiments reveal that multi-task full fine-tuning is the strongest operational default at every model size we test. Specialist models are strong on their target tasks but often degrade sharply off-task, making reliable routing important. Sequential Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) preserves earlier skills better than sequential full fine-tuning, while merging a specialist with its base model improves off-task robustness with limited same-task loss for larger models. We conclude with practical guidelines for selecting fine-tuning strategies in real-world settings.

paper.title: Capable yet Parsimonious: Extracting and Characterizing Hidden Chain-of-Thought in Frontier Models

We find that Astra exhibits token-efficient directed reasoning, selecting a correct trajectory earlier, while resolving elementary steps internally and externalizing only crucial reasoning. paper.title: Return or Revise? Learning When Revision Helps Retrieval-Augmented QA

paper.title: TEMPS: Temporal Sentence Embeddings for Temporal Information Retrieval
paper.summary: Modern information retrieval (IR) systems rarely represent time, yet many information needs depend on it: in clinical, journalistic, and legal search, when an event occurred can decide whether a document is relevant. paper.title: MORSE: Multi-Context Ordering via Reverse Scoring for Evidence-Preserving Compression
paper.summary: Likelihood-based context compression can account for cross-context redundancy through sequential scoring, but this makes compression outcomes sensitive to context order. MORSE applies a common reverse query-evidence principle to both individual contexts and compressed candidate outputs, using the former to construct an evidence-first anchor and the latter to guide compression-aware permutation selection. Across multi-hop QA benchmarks, compression procedures, budgets, and scoring models, MORSE consistently improves evidence preservation over static reverse ordering and compute-matched random search, with corresponding overall improvements in downstream QA. paper.title: FLEET: From Logits Entropy to Enhanced Trajectories in Text Generation
paper.summary: Solutions based on large language models (LLMs) often rely on temperature sampling to improve accuracy and stability by aggregating multiple samples from the completion distribution. paper.title: Calibration as a First-Class Criterion in LLM Evaluation
paper.summary: Calibration of language models -- the alignment between expressed or implicit confidence and empirical correctness -- is a well-studied subfield within NLP. The problem is adoption: outside this subfield, NLP research regularly introduces new models, datasets, and benchmarks without checking whether the model's confidence scores are meaningful. We argue that this adoption gap is a major obstacle to trustworthy LLM evaluation. Miscalibration causes problems in two distinct areas: at deployment, where overconfident mistakes cause real harm, and inside the research pipeline, where methods like LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic data generation, and active learning rely on calibrated confidence without verifying it. Standard calibration metrics only require two inputs per example: a confidence score and a correctness judgment. Most benchmarks in use today already provide both, meaning calibration can be reported immediately. For open-ended generation, however, defining these two inputs is still an open challenge. We argue that each NLP subfield should pair its main performance metric with a calibration score and call for treating calibration as an essential property of every model rather than a niche topic.

paper.summary: Representation Autoencoders (RAEs) enable diffusion models to operate in the feature spaces of pretrained visual encoders. However, many off-the-shelf encoders are not optimized for faithful reconstruction, discarding fine-grained visual details. As expected, finetuning these encoders for image reconstruction recovers such details. However, perhaps counterintuitively, this procedure reduces the effective dimensionality of the resulting representation, and the altered geometry has downstream effects on generation. Specifically, we show that using the standard velocity prediction in flow matching in this high-dimensional space requires the model to fit orthogonal noise directions outside the low-dimensional signal manifold, making optimization inefficient. This motivates using the clean data parameterization (x_{0}-prediction) instead, which focuses learning on the underlying signal manifold. Across experiments with multiple strong-reconstruction encoders, we show that x_{0}-prediction consistently improves text-to-image generation performance.

paper.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis Needs a Group Action
paper.summary: To make claims about representations that generalize beyond a particular trained model, we need to specify when two representations should count as equivalent. The Linear Representation Hypothesis is often discussed without making this equivalence explicit. Different notions of equivalence preserve different structures, so metrics, probes, and interventions that appear to study the same representation may in fact correspond to different hypotheses. We therefore argue that the Linear Representation Hypothesis is not one hypothesis but a family of claims distinguished by representation equivalence. We formalize this idea using group actions, specifying the representation object, the procedure that produces it, and the property ultimately asserted, while accounting for equivalences imposed by the model architecture. This framework clarifies how assumptions can change across metrics, reading points, and analysis stages, and we use it to audit common representation quantities and recent interpretability analyses.

paper.title: PackLab: A Comprehensive Framework for Developing, Training, and Evaluating MLLMs in Robotic Bin Packing
paper.summary: Robotic bin packing requires long-horizon sequential decision-making, as each object placement affects the available space for subsequent packing. Existing methods primarily rely on hand-crafted geometric heuristics that optimize predefined objectives or reinforcement learning policies learned through trial and error over predefined training configurations. Despite recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for this task, their potential for closed-loop sequential decisions across heterogeneous packing configurations remains underexplored. To address this gap, we introduce PackLab, a comprehensive framework for developing, training, and evaluating MLLMs for closed-loop robotic bin packing. PackLab-Suite provides a physics-based simulation platform for scalable generation of diverse training packing trajectories and evaluation of their physical outcomes. PackLab-VLM is a packing-specialized MLLM that understands the evolving object and container states to jointly select objects and predict placements in a closed-loop manner. PackLab-Bench provides standardized packing scenarios at multiple difficulty levels for systematic evaluation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, on average, PackLab-VLM outperforms conventional packing heuristics, traditional reinforcement learning methods, and general-purpose MLLMs across object sets and container configurations, highlighting the potential of MLLMs for long-horizon robotic packing. paper.title: Rate-distortion optimization for full-reference image quality metrics via stochastic Hessian estimates
paper.summary: Block-based video codecs select coding parameters based on the input by optimizing a rate-distortion trade-off. The conventional distortion choice, the sum of squared errors (SSE), simplifies parameter selection: the SSE is the sum of block-wise SSEs, so rate-distortion optimization (RDO) can treat blocks independently. Alternatively, full-reference image quality assessment (FR-IQA) metrics such as MS-SSIM or LPIPS often align better with the human visual system than SSE, but they cannot be used in-loop: they do not decompose block-wise and typically require the fully decoded image as input. Building on existing results in metric quadratization, we approximate a broad class of FR-IQA metrics by an input-dependent quadratic distortion (IDQD), whose quadratic form matrix is derived from the Hessian of the metric evaluated at the source video. To make the distortion computable block-wise, we propose two approximations of the Hessian matrix: 1) keeping the block-diagonal, and 2) keeping only its diagonal. We propose estimators for both that require only matrix-vector products with the Hessian obtained by automatic differentiation. Across five metrics for Kodak and CLIC in VVC, IDQD-RDO achieves 14.2-36.7 % BD-rate savings under the target metric with no decoder changes and incurs 10-30 % encoding complexity overhead.
